newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Renewed clashes leave Tajik ceasefire in tatters.
newsitem.headline: Renewed clashes leave Tajik ceasefire in tatters.

text.p: Four government soldiers were killed and 14 wounded in fresh clashes with opposition fighters in Tajikistan which left a brief ceasefire in tatters on Friday.
Russia's Interfax news agency said the clashes took place in Garm, some 150 km (100 miles) east of the capital Dushanbe.

Opposition radio monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation confirmed there had been new fighting in the remote, mountainous republic bordering Afghanistan and China but did not say exactly where the clashes were.
In Dushanbe, government security forces combed local buildings for bombs and mines after one person was killed and one injured in two explosions on Thursday.
It was not clear who planted the devices, but Russian Defence Council secretary Yuri Baturin told reporters in Dushanbe that more explosions could follow.
"There could be more provocations like those in Dushanbe yesterday but we must not give in to them," said Baturin, who was in Dushanbe to prepare the way for new ceasefire talks.

Interfax, citing well-informed sources in the Tajik interior ministry, said four government soldiers were killed and 14 wounded in the clashes, which breached a ceasefire supposed to have begun at midnight on Wednesday.
Previous ceasefires in the bloody four-year civil war in the former Soviet republic have been routinely flouted. A U.N.-sponsored truce reconfirmed in July collapsed almost as soon as it was signed.
Interfax said rebel forces had surrounded a battalion of Tajik interior ministry troops near Garm where fighting has continued sporadically for several days.
The agency said the guerrillas were hammering the battalion with anti-aircraft guns, automatic weapons and rocket-propelled grenades.
It said the fighters had sustained casualties but gave no further details.
The Tajik government issued a note of protest to the United Nations on Thursday, accusing opposition forces of violating the ceasefire.
Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri agreed on a ceasefire from midnight on Wednesday following peace talks in northern Afghanistan.
They are due to sign a peace accord in Moscow on December 19, but details of the agreement have not been made public.
